study type: Genetic Case Study with Family Segregation Analysis and Literature Review
exposure: Homozygous nonsense variant (c.1234C > T: p.Arg412*) in the ATP1A2 gene
Heterozygous state of the ATP1A2 gene variant
outcome: FARIMPD (Fetal akinesia, respiratory insufficiency, microcephaly, polymicrogyria, and dysmorphic facies) syndrome phenotypes
cohort: The participants included newborns and their parents from a particular family, along with control subjects.
finding: A specific ATP1A2 nonsense variant (c.1234C > T) is lethal in the homozygous state, causing FARIMPD syndrome and early death, but is compatible with infant survival and associated with migraine symptoms in the heterozygous state.
